_about: Every parameter of the IJSP revision experiment. provenance: measured = estimated from a named dataset; standard = published constant; assumed = chosen by the authors and varied in the sensitivity analysis.

fleet.provenance: assumed (as in the submitted manuscript, Table 1)

replications.provenance: assumed; 50 matches the submitted manuscript's 50 iterations; adequacy checked by CI half-width

vulnerabilities.lambda_provenance: assumed: NVD counts are not exposure rates, because CVE assignment for consumer products is sparse
vulnerabilities.real_pool: NVD CVE records 2021-2025 classified by domain (scripts/01_extract_nvd.py); CVSS v3.x C/I/A impact, attack vector, exploitability subscore and CWE are drawn jointly by resampling whole records
vulnerabilities.shrinkage_provenance: assumed: a record is drawn from the domain pool with probability n_d/(n_d+n0), else from the pooled consumer-IoT pool; protects small pools (healthcare n=17)
vulnerabilities.kev_provenance: assumed; KEV membership itself is measured (CISA KEV catalogue)
vulnerabilities.beta_provenance: assumed annual exploitation propensity of an exploitable vulnerability; p_v = min(1, beta * expl_v/3.9 * kev_mult)
vulnerabilities.cvss_impact_provenance: standard (FIRST CVSS v3.1 specification); normalised by 0.56

synthetic.provenance: assumed (simulated arm): attributes drawn independently and uniformly

weakness_classes._rule: a CVE takes the first class (in this order) that any of its CWEs belongs to; else OTHER

controls._provenance: catalogue drawn from ETSI EN 303 645 v3.1.3, NIST IR 8259A and NIST CSF 2.0; cost, latency, throughput and effectiveness values are assumed and varied in sensitivity analysis

list.name: Network segmentation (IoT VLAN, deny by default)

controls.latency_note: amortised per-message latency with session resumption (assumed); every control is individually feasible on every domain, combinations compete

effectiveness._meaning: e[k][class] = probability that control k neutralises a vulnerability of that weakness class (if applicable to its attack vector)

ids.rho_provenance: assumed: probability that a detected attack is stopped before impact
ids.class_to_cic_provenance: assumed mapping; memory/access/other exploits are delivered as crafted payloads, so the web-based (payload) category is used: it is also the lowest, i.e. conservative
ids.detection_source: measured: CIC IoT-DIAD 2024 packet features, conservative threshold at 1% benign FPR (scripts/03_cic_ids_detection.py)

privacy.collection_provenance: assumed share of collected personal data beyond what the service needs
privacy.storage_provenance: assumed probability that stored personal data is recoverable without encryption at rest
privacy.tp_baseline_real: measured: per-device encrypted share of application payload bytes, CIC IoT-DIAD 2024 benign captures (47 devices, scripts/02_cic_transfer_protection.py), resampled for every device

trust._meaning: technical trustworthiness PROXIES, not measured consumer perception
trust.consumer: TCB = 0.4 + 0.2*(x_k9 + x_k10 + x_k12) (transparency and accountability controls)

compliance._meaning: requirement coverage: share of applicable requirements whose control rule is met. A coverage indicator, not a legal determination.

GDPR.ref: Art 25 data protection by design and by default
Art 32(1)(b) ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience
Art 32(1)(d) regular testing and evaluation of measures

POPIA.ref: s19(2)(c)-(d) verify safeguards; update in response to new risks

NIST.ref: PR.AA identity management, authentication and access control
PR.DS data security (at rest and in transit)
RS.MA, RS.CO incident management and reporting

compliance.provenance: author mapping of requirement to control; requires expert legal validation before operational use

constraints.budget_meaning: fraction of the cost of deploying every applicable control on every device

optimizer.repair: per-device latency/throughput then global budget (drop lowest marginal-value-per-cost)
optimizer.stopping: fixed generation budget; convergence tracked by hypervolume
optimizer.representative: knee point: front member closest (Euclidean, objective-wise min-max normalised) to the ideal point
optimizer.exact_reference: weighted-sum MILP (HiGHS) over per-device enumerated feasible configurations, 11 weight vectors on the simplex lattice + equal weights

baselines.B1_checklist: ETSI EN 303 645 provision order (k1,k12,k3,k5,k4,k8,k9,k10,k6,k11,k7,k2) applied device by device until budget
baselines.B2_greedy_security: repeatedly add the feasible control with largest security gain per cost
baselines.B3_compliance_only: exact MILP maximising compliance coverage only
baselines.B4_random: random feasible additions until budget (mean of 200 draws)
baselines.B5_weighted_sum: exact MILP, equal weights on S,P,T,CS (single-objective scalarisation)

statistics.tests: Wilcoxon signed-rank, paired by replication, knee vs each baseline per objective; Holm correction within each baseline

existing_controls.k4_real_rule: real arm: k4 already deployed if the device's measured encrypted share >= 0.9; simulated arm: same prevalence as other controls
existing_controls.provenance: assumed prevalence (measured for k4 in the real arm); existing controls are sunk (no cost) and are never removed; if a drawn set breaks a device cap, controls are dropped in descending latency order until feasible
